findings.title: Browser launch failure leaves fixture servers open
findings.origin: inherited relative to HEAD; present in frozen inventories; panel additions do not introduce this gap
findings.reproduction: verification-odd-repro.mjs executes actual test declaration callbacks in a VM. Stub launch rejects; all six registered callbacks retain serverStillListening=true. No real browser or server is launched by this reproduction. Panel/research variants confirmed by source only.
findings.impact: A missing browser executable or launch error bypasses finally after a real server.listen, potentially hanging the test runner with an open listener. A rejection from browser.close also prevents subsequent server.close.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Declare browser before try; put launch/page setup inside try; nest server close in a finally around browser close, as already done in workspace-browser tests.
objections: No real browser failure run was authorised. Reproduction proves callback control flow using fakes, not OS process state.
Workspace harness cleanup tests pass for their nine callbacks; they do not cover these other harnesses.

findings.title: Focus assertions can pass for the wrong space-name input
findings.origin: inherited relative to HEAD; settings.test.mjs unchanged
findings.reproduction: verification-odd-repro.mjs creates two actual settings-dom fake inputs, focuses the first, verifies it differs from the second, then calls the unmodified assertFocused helper targeting the second. Assertion passes because both labels are <input>.
findings.impact: The new-space focus test can pass when focus stays on an existing space input. The helper cannot detect replacement of a focused input by another node with the same diagnostic label.
findings.smallestSafeFix: Assert boolean identity with assert.ok(page.document.activeElement === node, a short label-only diagnostic) to avoid serializing DOM graphs.
objections: This demonstrates test weakness, not a confirmed production focus regression.
Unique-ID controls do not have the same collision in these fixtures.

objections.detail: Fallback differential baseline is current source with one literal replacement, not a captured historical file. Currently replacement matches and differs, and all focused tests pass. If formatting changes, replacement silently returns current source and differential assertions compare identical code. VM reproduction proves this hypothetical failure mode; it is not a current vacuous result. Assert replacement occurred and record a captured baseline hash for stronger claims.

alarm(30) terminates the parent outside exception cleanup; the child pause loop can survive a late parent timeout. Source-only concern, not reproduced or compiled. Treat watchdog cleanup claims as unverified on timeout.

The expected HTML uses the current renderMessage function. Useful for streaming-vs-current-one-shot consistency and node identity, but cannot alone prove preservation against the historical renderer. Historical fixture is present and was read; no browser runs authorised.

Exact callback count 9 intentionally detects scope drift, but will require maintenance when workspace-browser adds cases. Two fake phases passed. This coverage is limited to that extracted declaration suffix.
Extracted helper source is exercised with owned synthetic children and fake token reads. Four tests passed. It does not exercise actual provider accounts or remote transport.

tests.safety: Read selected tests and relevant helpers first. Node request tests inject fetch and secrets, call only request, not config/view/list. Provider lifecycle extracts helpers and replaces spawn with owned Node dummy children; it does not launch Python provider server. Cleanup test uses disposable loopback listeners. Python download subprocess is mocked. No app, browser, real provider, profile, credentials, Keychain, PC, SSH, external network, benchmark, build, installation or publication.
